proposals.before: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, finding Chong a fatherless child, doted on him.
proposals.after: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
proposals.reason: 偏孤 cannot mean fatherless here because the father is still alive until the later mourning notice; it means left partially orphaned by his mother.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuancian.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuanjian.
proposals.reason: 元簡 should be romanized Yuanjian; Yuancian is an erroneous spelling.

proposals.before: Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wu commandery of Xing.
proposals.after: Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wuxing commandery.
proposals.reason: 吳興郡 is the commandery name Wuxing, not Wu commandery of Xing.

proposals.after: merit clerk in the two establishments of the Prince of Xuancheng.
proposals.reason: The unit completes 中軍宣[城]王二府功曹史 from the preceding line; the current English is only a broken fragment.

decisions.reason: s0007 武帝以沖偏孤 follows the mother's death in Qi; 偏孤 means half-orphaned (one parent lost). Father Maozhang is still identified as alive in s0006, so "fatherless" is wrong and "partially orphaned" matches the Chinese.
s0048 諡曰元簡: 元 is Yuan and 簡 is jian, so the posthumous name is Yuanjian; Yuancian is a misspelling and the rest of the sentence is unchanged.
s0097 監吳興郡 names the single commandery Wuxing (吳興); "Wu commandery of Xing" wrongly splits the toponym, and Wuxing commandery restores the correct place.

With s0131–s0132, the Chinese continues as 中軍宣[城]王二府功曹史; "[City] Wang." is a broken fragment, and the proposed completion correctly supplies Xuancheng and the merit-clerk office of the two establishments.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0002 restores the posthumous name as Yuanjian; claim c0003 still stored the erroneous English form Yuancian while zh/pinyin were already correct.
